checked_sources: independent_checks.py: Independent 2n−1 palette construction for each split n=4..14, direct rich-neighbor validation and exhaustive normalized K3,3 case.
correctness.rationale: The endpoints of any rich-edge set form a vertex cover of K_n,n, so at least one whole part is covered and |R|≥n. For n≥4, divide one part into d and n−d (each ≥2), choose disjoint palettes X,Y of n−1 and z, fill cyclic Latin rectangles on the two complementary blocks, and complete two center rows with unused colors and z. Checking incident color intersections shows exactly the n edges of two stars are rich and all edges have an adjacent distinct rich edge. Every rich edge forces at least 2n−1 colors. n=2 requires four all-distinct colors; for n=3 the exhibited five-color matrix gives exactly four rich edges, while any putative 3-rich set must be a star (rich-edge P4 impossible at 2n−1 colors) and then would force a K_3,2 proper coloring from only two unused colors, impossible. Independent direct edge-neighbor tests checked all splits for n=4..14; full normalized order-three five-color enumeration found minimum four, independently confirming but not replacing the all-n proof.
residual_risks: Finite tests alone do not prove infinite claims; source proof reconstructed and critical steps checked analytically.
